newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill rates rise on expected tightness.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill rates rise on expected tightness.

text.p: Philippine Treasury bill rates were higher in the secondary market after the central bank raised further the liquidity reserve to four percent from three percent, traders said.
The central bank's new ruling aimed to siphon pesos that may be used for peso speculation. It estimates liquidity will contract by 21.2 billion pesos.
Earlier in the week, the central bank had raised the liquidity reserve to three percent from two percent.
"We expect the market to tighten. It's (the central bank's new ruling) is not the end of it. He can still afford to increase some more," a foreign bank trader said.
The market, however, saw little activity as most banks turned sellers.
"Everybody's selling. Banks would like to shore up their liquidity," another trader said.
The average interbank call loan rate fell to 20.0625 percent from 22.03125 percent in reaction to the central bank's two percentage-point cut in the overnight borrowing rate to 20 percent.
Volume was higher at 16.84 billion pesos from 11.28 billion, with 23 lenders and 14 borrowers.
